extracted.intended_audience: researchers and journal editors interested in peer review incentives, scientometrics, and causal evaluation methods
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating the causal impact of peer-review accolade awards on reviewer behaviour (measured as number of reviews) using large-scale observational/quasi-experimental data (Publons) with PSM and DiD methods, including robustness and subgroup analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of motivation (quantity-focused)
rubrics_metrics.description: The study focuses on the quantity of reviews as the operationalization of 'motivation'. "In our study, we only focus on the quantity of reviews. The term 'motivation' in the following text also underscores the number of reviews."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or measuring reviewer motivation for this research task, treat annual number of reviews as the dependent variable rather than review quality; acknowledge that quality and quantity are distinct dimensions of reviewer motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of accolade awards as an incentive (theoretical expectations and risks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accolade awards are increasingly used to motivate reviewers due to cost-effectiveness and potential to align with prosocial and self-achievement motivations, but their effectiveness is uncertain and can produce both positive and negative effects (motivation crowding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both possible directions of effect: awards may increase motivation via recognition, or decrease intrinsic motivation via crowding out, diminished marginal utility, or unexpected-award effects. Cite literature on monetary vs non-monetary rewards and motivation crowding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-natural experiment design using platform awards as treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use platform-identified award winners (Publons Global Peer Review Award) as the experimental/treatment group and non-winners as the control group to form a quasi-natural experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a single award cohort for primary analysis (here 2018) to avoid heterogeneous multi-period DiD issues; exclude winners from adjacent years from the control group; complement with robustness analyses using other award years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propensity score matching (PSM) to construct a comparable control group
rubrics_metrics.description: PSM is used to create a control group resembling the experimental group. "The single-period matching method is adopted, which typically focuses on the first period (2012) as the matching period." Matching variables include academic age, gender, discipline, cumulative publications, and cumulative citations; MatchIt nearest neighbor non-parametric method is employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match on baseline (pre-treatment) covariates; use nearest-neighbor or equivalent; perform balance tests post-matching; choose the earliest period available for matching to capture baseline characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching balance assessment using Standardized Mean Difference (SMD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance of matching is assessed via standardized mean difference (SMD). "If the SMD of the variables is below 0.05 or 0.1, it suggests a good matching effect."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report SMD for each covariate before and after matching; aim for SMD < 0.1 (preferably < 0.05); visualize balance (e.g., love plot) and document any variables with SMD > thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference-in-differences (DiD) estimation with interactive fixed effects
rubrics_metrics.description: DiD (implemented with the fect package) is used to estimate the causal impact. The estimator includes interactive fixed effects (two-way fixed effects) and controls. Example formula presented: R_{i,t} = β1 DiD_{i,t} + β2 P_{i,t-1} + ... + year_t + u_i + δ_{i,t}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement DiD with appropriate fixed effects (two-way/interactive); include control covariates and year dummies; use software packages that support interactive fixed effects for panel DiD (e.g., fect in R).

rubrics_metrics.name: DiD assumption — Linear Assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The DiD is based on the 'Linear Assumption', that the treatment effect changes at a constant rate throughout the study period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a constant-rate change assumption is reasonable for the treatment effect in the studied timeframe; consider alternative specifications if effect heterogeneity over time is suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: DiD assumption — Parallel Trend Assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Parallel Trend Assumption' requires that both the control group and the experimental group exhibit similar trends before treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visually and statistically assess pre-treatment trends; if parallel trends do not hold, use methods to improve comparability (e.g., better matching, synthetic controls, interactive fixed effects) or interpret with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-trend and equivalence testing: F-test and TOST
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the F test for pre-trend testing and TOST (equivalence) tests included in fect. "A higher p-value from the F-test suggests a better fit of the parallel trend... A smaller p-value for the TOST indicates a better fit to the pre-trend."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both F-test and TOST results; interpret F p > 0.05 as supportive of no pre-trend differences and small TOST p-values as supportive of equivalence within chosen bounds; specify equivalence ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placebo (falsification) tests via fictitious treatment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Fictionalize treatment time (e.g., one or two years before actual award) and rerun DiD; the fictitious treatment should not generate significant ATTs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform placebo tests for 1–2 pre-treatment years; expect non-significant DiD estimates and supportive F/TOST results; significant placebo effects indicate possible bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent variable specification: annual number of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The dependent variable is the annual number of reviews conducted by reviewers (from Publons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and document how review counts are measured (platform coverage limitations); use consistent annual windows; consider robustness to alternative aggregation (e.g., counts per year vs rolling windows).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of treatment indicator (DiD variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: DiD independent variable indicates whether the individual is an accolade award winner and the year is after 2018 (post-treatment). Winners are pre-treatment in years 2012–2017 and treated from 2018 onward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly define treatment timing and coding; exclude other winners from control; ensure consistent treatment start across treated units for single-period DiD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control variables to reduce confounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Control for prior-year number of publications, cumulative citations, academic age, interactions (academic age × cumulative publications and academic age × cumulative citations), interdisciplinarity (number of second-level disciplines), and social capital (number of collaborators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include bibliometric and career-stage covariates that plausibly affect both likelihood of winning and review activity; justify inclusion and test sensitivity to alternative control sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalizing academic age
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic age is determined according to the year of a scholar's first publication and is included as a control/stratifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute academic age consistently across datasets (use earliest publication year); consider interactions of academic age with productivity/citations to proxy seniority effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinarity metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Interdisciplinarity is quantified by the number of second-level disciplines of a scholar's outputs (OpenAlex-derived).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standardized classification (e.g., OpenAlex categories) and report how multiple-discipline authors are counted; use as a control or moderator for awarding effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy for social capital: collaborator count
rubrics_metrics.description: A scholar's social capital is proxied by the number of their collaborators determined from co-authorship (number of authors in publications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute collaborator counts from publication metadata; include as control and as moderator in subgroup analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name disambiguation and identifier linkage best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Linking across ResearcherIDs, MAGIDs, ORCIDs, and OpenAlexIDs is necessary; use golden name-disambiguation datasets (LAGOS-AND primary, OpenAIRE and EMAKG supplementary) leveraging DOIs and ORCIDs to reduce ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude ResearcherIDs not self-registered in ORCID to reduce ambiguity; use DOI-based matching blocks for high-precision linking; document disambiguation steps and rely on established gold datasets where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data integration: assemble panel dataset and timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a panel dataset of reviewers with annual review and bibliometric data. Example here: panel 2012–2023; pre-treatment period 2012–2017; post-treatment 2019–2023; treatment year 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose pre/post windows to ensure sufficient pre-treatment trend assessment and post-treatment outcome observation; avoid heterogeneous multi-period complications when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing data beyond the platform (coverage concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address missing review records not linked to Publons by reasoning about whether coverage changes affect experimental and control groups similarly; if coverage (C) affects both groups similarly (C2−C1 equal), missing data unlikely to bias inference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess plausibility that missingness evolves similarly across groups; conduct sensitivity analyses or document assumptions; provide schematic hypotheses and argue cases where missing data would bias results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform robustness analyses including re-running the PSM-DiD using winners from other years (2017 and 2019) and other specification checks; findings should follow similar patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report results for alternative cohorts, alternative matching/caliper choices, alternative sets of controls, and model specifications to show stability of estimated effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heterogeneity/subgroup analyses of individual differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore moderating effects of academic age, seniority, funding, social capital, interdisciplinarity, and gender on the awarding effect; use moderating-effect models, subgroup modeling, and Wald tests for coefficient differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify moderators of interest; use interaction terms or subgroup regressions; use statistical tests (e.g., Wald) to compare DiD coefficients across groups and report which moderators produce significant differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Socio-economic moderator analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess socio-economic moderators such as official language (English usage), Confucian culture, pro-active tendencies (country-level reviews), income level, and national scientific performance (average H-index) via subgroup analyses and Wald tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect country-level indicators and run subgroup DiD or interaction models; interpret which country-level conditions mitigate or exacerbate the award effect (e.g., English-speaking, high-income, high H-index mitigate negative effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of ATT and temporal patterning
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot average treatment effects on the treated (ATTs) over time to inspect dynamics; here ATTs are around −4 after treatment with a V-shaped pattern (decline for four years then slowing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present ATT time series with confidence intervals; interpret magnitude and temporal shape (e.g., immediate drop, rebound, long-run effects) rather than only aggregate coefficient; relate dynamics to proposed mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism articulation: marginal utility, voluntary work, unexpected awards, and social sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed mechanisms for negative awarding effects include diminishing marginal utility of awards, the voluntary nature of peer review reducing incentive appeal, unexpected-award dynamics, and possible peer social sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observed heterogeneity (e.g., stronger negative effects for men, senior reviewers, high social capital) and supplementary literature to argue mechanism plausibility; where possible, test mechanisms directly or with mediators.
